title: Add polynomials by collecting like terms ((x² + 2x − 4) + (2x² − 3x − 4) = 3x² − x − 8)

lesson.title: Adding Polynomials: Team Up the Like Terms

steps.say: You already know how to combine like terms, like turning zero point five n minus three n plus twenty five into negative two point five n plus twenty five. Today we use that same move to add two whole polynomials together. The trick is simple: like terms team up, unlike terms stay apart.

Think of each polynomial as a pile of algebra tiles. The first pile has one x squared tile, two x tiles, and four negative unit tiles. The second pile has two x squared tiles, three negative x tiles, and four negative unit tiles. Adding means pushing both piles together into one big pile. Nothing disappears, nothing gets multiplied, we just have more tiles.

visual.caption: Tile counts in each pile: 1, 2, 4 and 2, 3, 4

steps.say: Now sort the big pile by tile type. Put the x squared tiles together: one plus two makes three x squared. Put the x tiles together: two positive x tiles and three negative x tiles. Two of them cancel in zero pairs, leaving one negative x. Put the unit tiles together: negative four plus negative four makes negative eight. Sorting by type is exactly collecting like terms.

visual.caption: After sorting: three x², one negative x, eight negative units

steps.say: Write down what each group became. Three x squared, then negative one x, which we just write as minus x, then minus eight. Let us double check the coefficients: one plus two is three, two minus three is negative one, negative four minus four is negative eight. So the sum is three x squared minus x minus eight.

visual.caption: Row 1 is the first polynomial, row 2 the second. Add each column: 3, −1, −8.

steps.say: Two traps to avoid. Trap one: adding the exponents. Some people see x squared plus two x squared and write three x to the power of four. No! Adding tiles never changes the tile's shape. Three x squared tiles are still x squared tiles, so the exponent stays two. Trap two: mixing unlike terms. You cannot squash negative x and negative eight into negative nine x. An x tile and a unit tile are different shapes, so they stay as separate terms.

visual.caption: Three separate groups means three separate terms in the answer

steps.say: Here is the whole thing in one line. Adding polynomials means stacking up the like terms, adding their coefficients, and leaving the exponents exactly as they are.

lesson.answer: Add like terms by adding their coefficients. The exponent stays the same, and unlike terms stay separate.

practice.question: Two rectangular garden beds at a community garden in Surrey have areas given by polynomials in square metres. The first bed has area two x squared plus five x plus three, and the second has area x squared minus two x plus six. Sketch each area as an area model split into an x squared part, an x part, and a unit part, then add the two polynomials to find the total area in square metres.
practice.answer: 3x² + 3x + 9 square metres (x² terms: 2 + 1 = 3; x terms: 5 − 2 = 3; constants: 3 + 6 = 9)
